title: Device identity, pairing, and revocation
objective: Implement device identity, one-time pairing, and revocation against the frozen SG-000052 relay contract without granting remote authority: protected local device key, public device identity, challenge and response, high-entropy short-expiry one-time pairing codes with rate limiting, key rotation, connection epochs, hard revoke, principal-wide revoke, all-route revoke, and emergency revoke and recovery semantics.

include: protected local device key with the private key never leaving the device
public device identity and challenge and response authentication
one-time pairing with high-entropy codes, short expiry, and rate limiting
hard revoke, principal-wide revoke, all-route revoke, and emergency revoke and recovery semantics
device-verifiable authorization envelope binding authenticated principal, connection, selected device, request digest, epoch, and session context
negative tests proving a compromised relay cannot remap principal A onto device B
exclude: any device uplink networking beyond the frozen contract vocabulary (SG-000055)
any new local MCP tool, tool schema change, capability widening, or approval change
any P16 tool-surface widening or provider submission
any public provider submission, directory publication, or availability claim

authority_delta.filesystem: None beyond the protected device-key store defined here.
authority_delta.secrets: Device key material is created and held under the existing protected-state boundary; no new secret class is exposed to tools.

invariants: the private device key never leaves the device and is never returned by any tool
the remote provider cannot create or replace device identity
pairing alone grants no workspace trust and no action approval
revocation invalidates active and refreshable sessions, not only UI state
the SG-000052 frame, envelope, failure, and bound vocabulary stays frozen

acceptance.claim: Protected local device key, public device identity, and challenge and response authentication work with key rotation and connection epochs.
One-time pairing enforces high entropy, short expiry, one-shot consumption, and rate limiting, and pairing grants no trust or approval by itself.
Hard, principal-wide, all-route, and emergency revocation invalidate active and refreshable sessions, and envelope tests prove no principal-A-to-device-B remap.
Exact-head CI including release qualification and supply-chain audit, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000054: OAuth 2.1 authorization boundary may proceed only after SG-000053 closes with device identity, pairing, and revocation qualified.

done_when: Device identity, pairing, and revocation are canonical with remap-proof envelope tests and no remote authority.
